Hi Rafael,

Thanks for sending the first pass of the SIG spreadsheet earlier. We reviewed pages 4–6 and have a few clarifying questions before we mark items as complete: 

1) Retention windows: You state that prompt logs are retained for up to 30 days by default, but the SIG row also references a 90-day troubleshooting window in some regions. Can you confirm exactly what is retained for 30 vs 90 days (raw prompts, generation outputs, KV caches, redaction artifacts)?

2) Training opt-out: Does Redwood ever train on customer prompts/outputs by default? If some customers opt out, can you describe the enforcement and audit trail?

3) Access controls & audit logs: For the logs that are retained, what role-level access exists and what is the retention of the audit trail?

We attached an updated SIG sheet (Medisys_SIG_v3.xlsx) with inline comments. If you can provide a short mapping document and any supporting artifacts (diagrams, attestations), that would help our security reviewers.

Best,
Alice Hart
Head of Vendor Security – Medisys Health

Alice —

Thanks for the detailed notes and the updated SIG. Quick answers up front, and I'll loop in our security SME with artifacts: 

- Retention windows: Default prompt & response logs (for hosted API customers) are retained 30 days for operational debugging. In specific enterprise contracts (regional data controls or SOC-driven exceptions) we can extend to 90 days — that extension applies to parsed/structured logs used for troubleshooting and not to raw third-party-hosted backups. KV cache snapshots are ephemeral and kept only for active sessions; we do not write persistent KV caches to long-term storage by default.

- Training opt-out: Redwood does not train models on customer prompts/outputs by default for customers who select the Privacy & No-Training option. We maintain an opt-out flag at the account level; once set, prompts/outputs are excluded from model training pipelines and we surface an audit record of the opt-out event.

- Audit trails & access: Audit logs for access to retained logs are kept for 365 days by default and available to customers as part of Dedicated/Private offerings or as an add-on for Hosted. Role-based access is enforced via RBAC; only engineers with the "support-debug" role (limited scope) can pull session logs, and each access event is logged.

I'm attaching a short answers PDF for your reviewers and will let Neha share the architecture diagram and the extract we promised.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — Rafael, thanks for the pointer. Adding details from Security and Controls below. I've included a small ASCII diagram inline and attached the retention diagram.

Summary:
- Prompts/outputs: Hosted API (default)
  - Collection: At ingress, request payloads are written to an encrypted short-term log (AES-256).
  - Retention: 30 days for operational logs. 90-day retention is an enterprise contract option; it applies to sanitized troubleshooting exports.
  - Training: By default, customer data is NOT included in training corpora unless the customer enables "allow-training" via account settings. If "allow-training" is on, model training pipelines consume data only after automated PII redaction and human review safeguards for flagged content.

- KV cache & ephemeral state:
  - KV caches are in-memory and evicted on session termination. We do NOT persist Kv cache contents to long-term object storage.

- Access & audits:
  - Access: Two-person authorization for any retrieval beyond automated retention windows.
  - Audit retention: 12 months standard for Hosted; 5 years for Dedicated under contract.

Quick ASCII of flow (simplified):
[Client] -> [Ingress LB] -> [Service (encrypt at rest)] -> [Short-term log (30d)]
                                    |-> [KV cache (ephemeral)]
                                    |-> [Troubleshooting export (90d if enterprise)]

Attached: retention-diagram.png (visual), redwood-sig-answers-v1.pdf (answers).

If Medisys needs a signed attestation for the opt-out enforcement flow, we can generate a scoped statement for the contract.

- Neha
